title: Commercial HMO straight-tip catheter denials: units the customer may be charged for, Urology and Continence Supply Program
content:
On the Continence Commercial HMO Program of the Urology and Continence Supply Program, the plan may deny the claim line of the program's latest straight-tip intermittent catheter (A4351) refill. The denial code then decides how many of that refill's units are concerned, that is, how many may become the customer's to pay.

For a straight-tip CO-151 denial on the Commercial HMO tier that this policy settles, and only for such a denial, the denial is handled as a non-covered amount only when no over-limit justification record is on file for the program, and a denial whose records on file are all dated after the date of service is absorbed by Larkfield; every other denial that is not appealed is still handled as a non-covered amount under the liability notice rule.

## Route by denial

| Denial on the refill's original claim | Units concerned |
|---|---|
| CO-151 (quantity not supported), and no over-limit justification record on file for the program | replaced by the refill's excess over the limit |
| PR-204 (not covered under the plan) | replaced by all of the refill's units |
| CO-151 with an over-limit justification record dated on or before the ship date | stay none: the denial goes to appeal |
| CO-151 whose over-limit justification records are all dated after the ship date | stay none: it is Larkfield's write-off |
| CO-197 (authorization absent) | stay none: the denial goes to appeal, because a refill ships only on an authorization grant valid on its ship date |
| any other code | stay none |

The refill concerned is the program's straight-tip refill with the latest ship date, and its denial is the denial posted against its original claim.

## Worked figures (hypothetical refill of 200 units with an excess over the limit of 50)

- CO-151 with no over-limit record on file: 50 units concerned.
- PR-204: all 200 units are concerned.
- CO-151 with an over-limit record dated on or before the ship date: no unit is concerned, and the denial goes to appeal.
- CO-197: no unit is concerned.
